title: Hiking
statementMd:
A traveler is planning a water hike along the river. He noted the suitable rest points for the night and wrote out their distances from the starting point. Each of these locations is further characterized by its *picturesqueness*, so for the $*i*$-th rest point the distance from the start equals $*x*_{*i*}$, and its *picturesqueness* equals $*b*_{*i*}$. The traveler will move down the river in one direction, we can assume that he will start from point $0$ on the coordinate axis and rest points are points with coordinates $*x*_{*i*}$.

Every day the traveler wants to cover the distance $*l*$. In practice, it turns out that this is not always possible, because he needs to end each day at one of the resting points. In addition, the traveler is choosing between two desires: cover distance $*l*$ every day and visit the most picturesque places.

Let's assume that if the traveler covers distance $*r*_{*j*}$ in a day, then he feels frustration ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/9ba75d666dbd9b44a6f7b0ee0e58dfb2d7b2d3dd.png), and his total frustration over the hike is calculated as the total frustration on all days.

Help him plan the route so as to minimize the *relative total frustration*: the total frustration divided by the total picturesqueness of all the rest points he used.

The traveler's path must end in the farthest rest point.

## Input

The first line of the input contains integers $*n*, *l*$ ($1 ≤ *n* ≤ 1000, 1 ≤ *l* ≤ 10^{5}$) — the number of rest points and the optimal length of one day path.

Then $*n*$ lines follow, each line describes one rest point as a pair of integers $*x*_{*i*}, *b*_{*i*}$ ($1 ≤ *x*_{*i*}, *b*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{6}$). No two rest points have the same $*x*_{*i*}$, the lines are given in the order of strictly increasing $*x*_{*i*}$.

## Output

Print the traveler's path as a sequence of the numbers of the resting points he used in the order he used them. Number the points from 1 to $*n*$ in the order of increasing $*x*_{*i*}$. The last printed number must be equal to $*n*$.

## Note

In the sample test the minimum value of *relative total frustration* approximately equals 0.097549. This value can be calculated as ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/bad16faba2aa8ac4e81ca909b5e927a7f644c23f.png).
statementZhMd:
一位旅行者计划沿河进行徒步旅行。他记录下了适合夜间休息的地点，并写下了这些地点到起点的距离。每个地点还有一个 *风景优美程度* 属性：对于第 $*i*$ 个休息点，它到起点的距离为 $*x*_{*i*}$，其 *风景优美程度* 为 $*b*_{*i*}$。旅行者将沿河向一个方向前进，我们可以认为他从坐标轴上的点 $0$ 出发，而休息点就是坐标为 $*x*_{*i*}$ 的点。

旅行者每天希望行走距离 $*l*$。但实际上这并不总是可行，因为他需要每天在某个休息点结束行程。此外，旅行者还需要在两个愿望之间进行选择：每天行走距离 $*l*$，以及游览风景最优美的地点。

假设旅行者某天行走了距离 $*r*_{*j*}$，那么他会感到沮丧 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/9ba75d666dbd9b44a6f7b0ee0e58dfb2d7b2d3dd.png)，整个旅程中的总沮丧值等于所有天的沮丧值之和。

请帮助他规划路线，使 *相对总沮丧值* 最小：总沮丧值除以他使用的所有休息点的风景优美程度之和。

旅行者的路线必须在最远的休息点结束。

## 输入格式

输入的第一行包含整数 $*n*, *l*$（$1 ≤ *n* ≤ 1000, 1 ≤ *l* ≤ 10^{5}$）——休息点的数量以及每天行程的理想长度。

接下来 $*n*$ 行，每行包含两个整数 $*x*_{*i*}, *b*_{*i*}$（$1 ≤ *x*_{*i*}, *b*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{6}$），表示一个休息点。不存在两个休息点具有相同的 $*x*_{*i*}$，且这些行按照 $*x*_{*i*}$ 严格递增的顺序给出。

## 输出格式

按照使用顺序，输出旅行者路线中所使用的休息点编号序列。按照 $*x*_{*i*}$ 递增的顺序，将休息点编号为 1 到 $*n*$。输出的最后一个编号必须等于 $*n*$。

## 说明

在样例测试中，*相对总沮丧值* 的最小值约为 0.097549。该值可以按照下式计算：![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/bad16faba2aa8ac4e81ca909b5e927a7f644c23f.png)。
